en: The bone belongs to one dog. It is the ___ bone.
One dog owns the bone, so we add ’s: dog’s.
Two girls each have a bag. They are the ___ bags.
There are many girls, so the apostrophe goes after the s: girls’.
The scarf belongs to Sam, so we write Sam’s.
The toys belong to the children. They are the ___ toys.
“Children” does not end in s, so we add ’s: children’s.
One rabbit has a fluffy tail. It is the ___ tail.
One rabbit owns the tail, so we add ’s: rabbit’s.
Three owls share one tree. It is the ___ tree.
There are three owls, so the apostrophe goes after the s: owls’.
The book belongs to one teacher, so we write teacher’s.
Which shows that the game belongs to Ben?
One owner called Ben, so we add ’s: Ben’s.
Lots of horses live in this field. It is the ___ field.
Many horses share the field, so the apostrophe goes after the s: horses’.
’s after “girl” means one girl owns the cake.

example.why_en: One dog owns the bone, so we add ’s: dog’s.

en.title: Whose is it?
en.teach: An apostrophe shows who something belongs to. One owner: add ’s (the dog’s bone). Many owners ending in s: add just ’ (the girls’ bags).
